video.title: The Only Playbook You Need to Sell Anything Online

summary: Chris Koerner presents a two-day playbook for growing an audience with short-form content, collecting email addresses, and selling digital products or services. He describes selling recordings from consulting sessions as a $97 Google Drive product and walks through GoHighLevel workflows for Instagram comments, lead magnets, email, and AI voice agents. He also demonstrates building a basic bank-statement-to-P&L app with AI Studio and discusses selling automation services or software. His recurring advice is to test content and offers, build an owned email list, and publish before over-planning.

speakers.description: Koerner Office host and presenter of the playbook.

ideas.name: Recorded social-media playbook sold as a digital product
ideas.one_liner: Package recorded consulting sessions and tactical material in a Google Drive folder, then sell access to an email list.
ideas.customer: People seeking practical advice on growing a brand and creating social content.
ideas.problem: They want practical guidance on hooks, retention, platform differences, and finding customers.
ideas.offer: A link to recordings and material in a Google Drive folder; no community or moderators.

pricing.notes: The product grew from recordings of one-on-one consulting.

acquisition_channels.details: Chris sent A/B-tested emails to segments of his newsletter. He says he did not promote this product on Twitter or elsewhere.

quote.text: I sent a bunch of AB test emails to my newsletter, and I ended up just selling a link to the Google Drive.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Chris recorded one-on-one Zoom consulting sessions, saved the recordings in Google Drive, and emailed buyers a link.
unit_economics_claims: Chris says the product made $120,000 profit in roughly 30 or 45 days.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; the recordings already existed when he sold them.

acquisition.how: Segmented email sends and A/B tests can be scheduled, but list building and offer decisions need human work.

onboarding.how: A payment and automated email can deliver the folder link.

delivery.how: The buyer receives a digital link without ongoing human fulfillment.

billing.how: Checkout and receipts can be automated; refunds and unusual cases need review.

support.how: Routine access questions can be handled with help pages or an agent, with human review for edge cases.

uk_applicability.notes: Digital files and email sales can work in the UK; UK privacy, consumer and tax obligations still apply.

risks: Sales depend on having an email audience and a relevant offer.
A platform ban can disrupt audience access if the seller has not built an owned list.

quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Turn existing expertise into a low-friction digital product
steps: Review existing recordings, notes, and files for material that solves a customer problem.
Package the useful material in a simple digital format, such as a Google Drive folder.
Test subject lines with A/B emails to relevant newsletter segments.
Deliver the link directly after purchase.

quote.text: I ended up just selling a link to the Google Drive. That's it, not like a community with moderators
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test content formats and keep separate research and posting accounts
steps: Test formats such as carousels, infographics, picture posts, and talking-head videos.
Track both positive platform signals and whether you enjoy making the content.
Use a separate research account to train the feed toward your niche and collect content examples.
Keep the posting account focused; use a separate personal account for unrelated viewing.

quote.text: I have like a consumption Instagram account for research. And then I have a posting Instagram account from posting
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a hook and withhold the promised payoff until the end
steps: Open with a visual or verbal hook that identifies the audience and promises a specific payoff.
Explain the situation and what you tried without revealing the key answer immediately.
Show evidence or a result, then deliver what the opening promised.
Use a call to action that fits the platform and the offer.

quote.text: And the whole time they're like, what is the thing? What, why are you hiding the idea?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Ask followers what they need before building a product
steps: Use an Instagram story poll to ask what problem followers have.
Follow up with another poll or question about the leading problem.
Repeat for several days to learn the specific product or solution they want.
Test the offer before making a large product investment.

quote.text: You don't have to guess what they want. So then when you have a big launch a month later
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Send social viewers to one simple email landing page
steps: Use a single focused landing page instead of a link page with many choices.
Ask for an email address first; collect additional details later if needed.
Use a clear lead magnet that is more valuable than the short video preview.
Send a short welcome sequence, then one relevant, valuable email each week.

quote.text: The more there is for them to click on the landing page, the more likely they are to get distracted and to never convert at all.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build a comment-to-lead workflow
steps: Connect the Instagram account in GoHighLevel through Facebook integrations.
Choose the specific post and use a trigger phrase with a contains-phrase filter.
Track first-level comments only.
Like the comment and rotate several public replies to reduce repetitive-looking responses.
DM a clickable button to the landing page, then capture the email and deliver the lead magnet.

quote.text: you want to be sure it's just contains and not exact match.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Keep a simple lead workflow and add tags
steps: Start with the trigger and one useful response instead of adding unnecessary complexity.
Tag each contact by the lead magnet or topic they requested.
Use tags later to send relevant offers to the right subset of contacts.
Build a thank-you page and a short delivery email, with a backup link on the page.

quote.text: If you have 30 different PDF lead magnets over the course of a year, and you tag all of those people that buy it as PDF
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Demonstrate the voice agent as part of a qualified lead journey
steps: Collect a phone number only when needed and include the required consent language.
Set an appropriate delay and condition in the workflow before an outbound call.
Train the voice agent for a narrow job, such as demonstrating itself to a business owner.
Invite interested prospects to a follow-up call with a real person.
Check applicable phone and marketing rules before using automated calls.

quote.text: your express goal is to get them on a call with me, a real human to further answer questions
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reuse a voice-agent template across clients
steps: Start from a marketplace template.
Replace the business name, voice, goals, availability, and knowledge base.
Connect the client's calendar and notifications.
Review call transcripts and update the prompt when the agent fails on repeated questions.
Duplicate a working configuration for the next client, then test the client-specific version.

quote.text: you literally just duplicate it. You just click that. Okay. Then you swap out the big and same with your new client.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Let AI improve a rough prompt and iterate on the prototype
steps: Write the idea in plain language, even if the prompt is rough.
Ask a separate AI tool to improve the prompt for the specific builder.
Build a first version and test it with dummy data.
Show the builder a screenshot and describe the specific change needed.
Do not treat a working prototype as proof that a regulated product is production-ready.

quote.text: the shortcut is to ask the AI, what to ask the AI.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Keep testing growth and offer variations
steps: Test different lead magnets, formats, offers, and workflow variations.
Keep successful versions running while testing new ones.
Make small changes and monitor what happens.
Do not assume a growth tactic will work indefinitely.

quote.text: Test all of it. Like, never ever ever stop testing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Publish and learn through execution
steps: Build a small version of the offer.
Publish it and observe real customer behavior.
Use the results to improve instead of spending too long researching or waiting for a mentor.

quote.text: You just have to ship the thing. You got to press publish.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Chris warns against spending too long researching, planning, and looking for mentors instead of publishing and learning from real execution.

quote.text: You just have to ship the thing. You got to press publish.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Treat content as repeated experiments: publish, learn from the signals, and keep improving rather than expecting one post to work.

quote.text: if you keep learning every time you post, you will eventually win.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Optimize short-form content for retention and a promised payoff, not just views or likes.

quote.text: If we publish a video that prevents people from swiping away to the next video and keeps people on our video for as long as possible
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Keep an account focused on the audience it has built; test a different niche with a new account if needed.

quote.text: You're the lawn mowing guy in their head now. It doesn't matter if they also like it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ask an audience about its problems before investing in a product.

quote.text: You don't have to guess what they want.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A small, loyal audience can be more valuable than a large, weakly engaged one.

quote.text: it's not about who you know, it's about who knows you and who trusts you.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use a focused landing page with a single clear next step to reduce friction.

quote.text: every piece of friction between you and the end goal, whether it's a free subscription to a newsletter or a $97, whatever
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Own an email relationship because a social platform can remove access to an audience.

quote.text: it's never been more important than ever to get emails, get people off the platform through landing pages, funnels
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use audience engagement to earn permission for a response; keep automation compliant with platform rules and applicable law.

quote.text: this middle step right here is the key to all of this being compliant. They have to comment
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use AI to get a first version made, then test it with real inputs and correct specific problems.

quote.text: any prompt is better than no prompt. You can level up your prompts after a while.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Publishing and selling teach faster than extended planning and research.

quote.text: you're going to learn 10 times faster by actually like selling and building than by like planning and researching and reading.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Keep successful experiments running while testing new variations; a tactic's performance may not last.

quote.text: don't just like rest on your laurels ... Keep moving. Keep testing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Chris describes his own digital-product sales, audience growth, and workflows with concrete examples and some specific numbers, but many platform metrics are anecdotal or unsupported, and several product ideas are hypothetical. Paulson's comments add software-promotion context rather than independent verification.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: GoHighLevel supports the channel, Chris says he uses it, promotes a trial link, and demonstrates its paid features. Chris also promotes TK Owners. The video includes a GoHighLevel trial promotion.
